issues.span: From this, they make a pile of stored-up goodness that is vastly greater, countless, and beyond measure.
issues.evidence: The sutra compares the donor's gift with the bodhisattva's patience: the bodhisattva's merit is vastly greater than that of the one who gives the worlds full of precious things. The children's text only hints at this with 'But'.
issues.fix: But an awakening hero might gain patience in this lesson on the teaching being without a self and not born. That hero makes a pile of stored-up goodness that is vastly greater than the gift, countless and beyond measure.

issues.span: Would that bunch of tiny specks be very large?
issues.evidence: Tibetan mang ba / academic 'numerous': the question is whether the collection of specks is many, not large.
issues.fix: Would that bunch of tiny specks be very many?

issues.span: ground all the earth in a world realm into powder. Imagine this world realm is a universe of a billion worlds.
issues.evidence: The earth particles are those in the whole universe of a billion worlds (three-thousandfold great thousandfold world system); calling it 'a world realm' and then redefining it is confusing.
issues.fix: Suppose they ground all the earth in a whole universe of a billion worlds into powder.
